newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's polished diamond exports down in June.
newsitem.headline: Israel's polished diamond exports down in June.

text.p: Israel's net exports of polished diamonds in June totalled $274 million, down from $279 million a year earlier, the Industry and Trade Ministry said on Wednesday.
In the first six months, net exports of polished diamonds rose to $2.092 billion from $1.956 billion a year earlier.
Exports of uncut diamonds totalled $96 million in June and $525 million in the first half, up 52 percent.
Total diamond exports amounted to $368 million in June, against $333 million in June 1996, while first-half exports rose to $2.617 billion from $2.303 billion a year earlier.

The ministry's supervisor of diamonds said in a statement that the sector's situation was worrisome. Israel's diamond dealers are purchasing far more expensive raw diamonds than in the past, importing both bigger and better quality stones.
Yet the dealers are selling the polished gems at only slightly above last year's prices, the statement said.
The number of workers in the industry is declining, both because bigger diamonds require fewer workers and because some manufacturers have shut down due to lack of profits.
